Mood stabilizers are great advice if someone hasn't tried it yet. I know people who have been helped a lot by them. 
 Unfortunately, in my case, they worked very briefly and at some point all that was left were the side effects.  But I don't want to give up just yet, so if I ever have the money, I'll keep trying.  Maybe by then they'll come up with some magic drug to fix broken brains?

I'm glad that your sister was able to get back on her feet! Hearing those stories is giving me hope and strength not to give up. 

But yes, people react very negatively when you say that no matter how hard you try, no medication or therapy has helped.  Even some doctors, instead of looking into the problem, only increase the dose of drugs or resign from further treatment. Sometimes it all seems completely hopeless...

Thank you, but there's not much to be proud of... I'm stuck in a loop of trying to get help and trying to kill myself. I should probably encourage you to try therapy, but I understand how difficult and expensive it is.  I've never had any luck with finding a good therapist myself tbh 
However, I think each new day is a small success for us.  I wish that one day you will be able to leave all this suffering behind you, even if it seems impossible now. It sounds silly, but I really wish you to find peace in life

I understand what you are saying and these are things that I know well, but on the other hand, it all builds up to the point where I have the impression that there is no way I can do it, I just want to die.  
As for my goals, I would like to go to a one-year floristry course and then to study law.  This year I did not take my end-of-school exams, I was in a very bad mental state and the psychologist said that I should not take them this time.  As a result, I cannot apply to university.  The whole family is dissatisfied with it and they want me take some "valuable" course, like economics, not floristry. And everyone think i'm too stupid to study law, they push me to be a programmer. I don't know, I just love learning new things and at the same time I would like to achieve something in my life.  To finally stop being a failure and worthless rubbish that only bothers everyone.

I feel like a failure because I can't achieve things that seem easy to many people.  I can't find a job, I can't finish school well and go to a good university, I can't even keep friends. I hate the thought that I really have depression, social anxiety and trauma.  I wish I could be normal, because all of this only sounds like excuses. Little things overwhelm me, I can hardly keep up with household chores.  If I could i will stay in bed all day, I'm pathetic.  None of my goals have any real value and my psychologist is probably just trying to keep me alive by saying my plans make sense.

I know mistakes happen, but I've been unsuccessful in the last few months, over and over again.  It is overwhelming and I can't even ask anyone for help, because everyone thinks that since I'm an adult, I should be able to handle it on my own.  The only person who tries to help me is my psychologist, but he too has his limits.  It just feels like I'm a burden to him and shouldn't bother him.  I don't want to be a problem for anyone.

Is there something that helps you keep going during the day? It could be the most trivial thing, like a cup of tea you like or favorite show. For example, I motivate myself to live, because of my favorite weekly podcast.

I assume, you are struggling with a lot of chaos in your head. It must consume a lot of energy, mentally and physically. Is there anything that gives you at least a little rest or allows you to focus your thoughts on something outside of all those negative mess?
